clue.text: Excited men on blown-up toys

parts.note: excited children are bouncy, full of jumping energy
castles are chessmen, the rooks

explanation.surface: Some excitable men are playing on inflatables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' points to chess pieces: a castle is the everyday name for a rook. 'on' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: These inflatable play structures are toys pumped full of air, so blown-up in the literal sense.

clue.text: Those not invited to the top celeb parties to meet the Queen? That's painful!

parts.words: Those not invited to the top celeb parties
parts.note: the B-list are second-tier celebrities, below the A-list who get the best invitations
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Second-rank celebrities, left out of the best parties, get to meet royalty instead, which hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A blister is a sore raised patch on the skin, something that hurts, so it is a painful thing.

clue.text: South African port, but not capital like Cape Town perhaps?

indicators.note: capital here is the capital, or upper-case, initial letter of the port, which is dropped

parts.note: Durban is a major port on South Africa's east coast

explanation.surface: A question about whether a South African port, not being the capital, resembles Cape Town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a seat of government, but it means the capital letter at the front of the port's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Town is a city, and city-like places are described as urban, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: See 1 across
Dictator demanding endless oil

indicators.note: the brand name loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: Castrol is a well-known brand of motor oil

explanation.surface: A tyrant insists on a supply of oil that never runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro ruled Cuba as an autocrat for decades, so he is an example of a dictator.

clue.text: One in Nepal, perhaps, from the mountains

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given may be arranged differently

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone in Nepal is probably a mountain person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like a hedge but it signals rearranging I (one) with NEPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine describes things belonging to high mountains, originally the Alps, so it means of the mountains.

clue.text: Child of eleven or twelve (precious troublesome range)

parts.note: precious in the sense of affectedly dainty means twee

indicators.note: troublesome suggests the following word is unruly and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A child on the edge of adolescence, both sweetly affected and difficult to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweenager is a child between childhood and the teens, roughly ten to twelve years old.

clue.text: See 16
Design of king or heretic on London's skyline?

indicators.note: a design of these words is a fresh arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: An image of a monarch or a heretic adorns the London skyline.
explanation.walkthrough: The Erotic Gherkin is a nickname of 30 St Mary Axe, the curved glass skyscraper in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This nickname refers to a tower block that stands out among the tall buildings of the City of London.

clue.text: Member at dance short of love

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the dance loses a letter

parts.note: the limbo is a dance done bending backwards under a bar
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone at a dance is without romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a member of the body, such as an arm or leg.

clue.text: Peeling off art to discover woven tapestries

indicators.note: woven suggests threads being interlaced into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restorers peel off a painting and find tapestries beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peeling off art' is a cheeky definition: the art of removing clothes one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: Striptease is the performance art of taking off clothes, garment by garment, so peeling off is apt.

clue.text: A heavy burden to have a lock at first, but no key

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A weighty problem: having a lock but no key to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a door key; the definition means a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music is written without any tonal centre, meaning it has no key.

clue.text: Tool didn't appear to be holding one back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled string is read in the reverse direction
holding means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: something that didn't appear wasn't there
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tool seemed not to be keeping hold of anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole string round, giving WASNONET read in reverse. 'to be' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a small stiff-backed saw used by carpenters for cutting joints, a tool.

clue.text: Suffering as a commuter (as in manipulated in scam)

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a scam is a trick

indicators.note: manipulated means handled and rearranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A commuter is suffering, perhaps having been manipulated in a con.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like an aside, but it is the wordplay; 'manipulated' rearranges AS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling nauseous on a train is a malady that strikes rail commuters, so it fits suffering as a passenger.

clue.text: Pint-sized, single, loveless boys with toys struggling to maintain sex appeal

parts.note: single is one, the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so one piece is held inside another
struggling implies writhing, so the remaining letters are jumbled
loveless removes love, the letter O, here from each of the two words

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Single boys without love, playing with toys, struggle to keep their charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' leaves BYS and TYS; 'struggling' rearranges them to TSYBSY, which holds IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Itsy-bitsy is a playful word meaning very small or tiny, so it means pint-sized.

clue.text: Commanders' story rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a saga is a long story

explanation.surface: The commanders' tale was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: An aga is an Ottoman military commander; the possessive 's in the definition is the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was a commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire, so the plural means commanders.

clue.text: Press finds the Guardian in the pub

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: PH is the abbreviation for public house on maps
this is a Guardian puzzle, so the paper refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: The press catches the Guardian in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' pretends to be journalism but is the verb. The Guardian means 'us' because the setter writes for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To press something is to push on it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Get the punters in, as pubs must — no dodgy food

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: A pub needs customers, so no more dodgy food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges PUBS MUST NO into PUTBUMSONS, followed by EATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting bums on seats is an idiom for attracting an audience or customers, as getting the punters in means.

clue.text: Shabby article containing Irish oath

indicators.note: containing means one word holds the others inside it

parts.note: the is the definite article
drat is a mild curse or oath

explanation.surface: A tatty article holds an Irish curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means of poor, inferior quality, which is what shabby means figuratively.

clue.text: Native American offensively risked being put off reservation, ultimately

indicators.note: put off suggests being thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately takes the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Native American took a risk in being expelled from the reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: This was once a common term for an American Indian, now regarded as an offensive slur.

clue.text: Dropping glass?

parts.note: a drinking glass whose name also describes someone or something that falls over

explanation.surface: Someone lets a glass fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed drinking glass bears this name, which also suggests something that falls down.

clue.text: Fruit — it's swallowed by political chum, but not entirely

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken inside the following word
not entirely means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a crony is a close friend, especially a favoured political ally
taken as written; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit gets partly eaten by a politician's friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A citron is a large citrus fruit like a thick-skinned lemon.

clue.text: More short and broad (small and fatter)

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
tubbier means fatter

explanation.surface: Someone describes a figure as shorter and wider, smaller and plumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubby means short and thick, so the comparative means more short and broad.

clue.text: See 27
Goddess hiding in refrigerator

indicators.note: hiding in says the answer is concealed within the word that follows

explanation.surface: A goddess concealed inside a fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of love poetry in Greek myth, a minor goddess.

clue.text: Kit with 19 to churn churned product

indicators.note: to churn is to stir vigorously, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the answer to 19 down, a drinking glass

explanation.surface: Equipment and a glass are needed to churn something made by churning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to churn' rearranges KIT plus TUMBLER, the answer to 19 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttermilk is the liquid left after cream is churned to make butter, so it is a churned product.

clue.text: Shaft appearing enormous in hospital department

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: A and E is accident and emergency, a British hospital department
XL is extra large, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A huge shaft turns up in a hospital emergency unit.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E (Accident and Emergency) is the British name for the emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or shaft on which a wheel turns.

clue.text: Maxim of Chinese philosophy in decline

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to sag is to droop or decline
yin is the passive principle in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A Chinese philosophical maxim is falling out of favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A saying is a short expression of wisdom, which is what a maxim is.

clue.text: You should be so lucky when flying or appearing nude in public?

definitions.meaning: a retort meaning that something is never going to happen

definitions.text: when flying or appearing nude in public?
definitions.meaning: flying and turning up naked in public are classic experiences while asleep

explanation.surface: A rebuff to someone hoping to fly or go naked in public.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a dismissive retort and the literal place where flying and public nudity occur, in sleep.
